## Paraguay's Chaco: dry forests, wildlife and vast distances

The [Chaco](/paraguay/place/chaco/) occupies a vast area of western [Paraguay](/paraguay/) beyond the Paraguay River. Outside the cities and farming districts, open woodland, savanna and plains stretch between settlements separated by long distances. Travelling through the Chaco highlights the change from the country's wetter east to open and sometimes extremely dry terrain.

The name **Gran Chaco** refers to a large natural region of South America extending beyond Paraguay into Argentina and Bolivia. An excursion into the Paraguayan Chaco therefore explores just part of this wider geographical area.

## What landscapes and habitats are found in the Chaco?

The Chaco cannot be reduced to a single picture of "dry steppe". The World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF) divides the Paraguayan Chaco into **dry and humid** zones. Thorn scrub, drought-adapted trees and open spaces dominate one area. Elsewhere, seasonally flooded lowlands, wet grasslands, palm savannas and water bodies appear.

The difference is especially noticeable between seasons. After rain, water may remain on the plains and attract birds. In the dry season, the same locations look entirely different. For planning, it is more useful to identify the specific part of the region than rely solely on the label "Chaco" in a tour description.

### Wildlife and birds

Numerous species of birds, armadillos, peccaries and other animals inhabit the region. WWF also highlights the conservation importance of surviving populations of native mammals. However, **sightings of wild animals cannot be guaranteed**: they depend on location, weather, time of day and animal behaviour.

Birdwatching generally requires patience, binoculars and knowledge of local habitats. Travellers interested in it should choose specific natural sites rather than relying on stops at urban attractions. Where protected areas can be visited, restrictions on movement and photography must be observed.

## Who lives in the Paraguayan Chaco?

Indigenous peoples with their own languages and traditions live here alongside Mennonite communities and residents of other settlements. The region's history includes migration, the development of agricultural land and the Chaco War between Paraguay and Bolivia in 1932–1935.

[Filadelfia](/paraguay/place/filadelfia/) is a useful place to learn about the Mennonite colonies. Its museums and cultural institutions cover local communities and nature. Indigenous peoples and Mennonite colonies have different histories and traditions; they should not be combined into one vague notion of "local colour". Visits to communities should be arranged with consent and respect for residents' privacy.

## Why road travel matters so much

The Chaco attracts travellers through its remoteness, but journeys require preparation. Road quality, fuel availability, communications and access to medical care change as you move farther from major settlements. Some dirt roads become difficult after heavy rain; in hot weather, water supplies and vehicle condition are especially important.

Before a long drive, check road conditions and which services are operating along the route. Drinking water, sun protection and insect repellent matter even for brief stops outside the vehicle. It is best to plan access to natural areas with local specialists.

## When should you visit the Chaco?

Weather differs between dry and humid parts of the region, so there is no single "best month" for all of the Chaco. Cooler months may be more pleasant for long walks, but the rainy season affects roads and access to natural areas. Some periods are intensely hot.

If birdwatching or visiting a particular lagoon is your main objective, choose dates around that site. An ordinary urban itinerary in [Asunción](/paraguay/place/asuncion/) requires much less travel time than reaching the Chaco's remote areas.

## Combining nature and history

One natural route links the Chaco with [Filadelfia](/paraguay/place/filadelfia/), where historical and natural-history museums can be visited. This allows travellers to explore both the region's biodiversity and its settlement history. Another format is an extended nature itinerary, stopping at water bodies and protected areas where access is permitted during the chosen season.

When comparing [Paraguay tours](/paraguay/tour/), look at the actual drives and time spent in the Chaco. Mentioning the region in a tour title does not in itself guarantee an in-depth nature experience.

## Frequently asked questions about the Chaco

### Is the Chaco a national park?

No. The Chaco is a large cross-border natural and geographical region, containing different settlements, agricultural areas and protected natural sites.

### Where is the Paraguayan Chaco?

West of the Paraguay River, on the broad plains of the country's western and northwestern regions.

### Can you see wild animals during an excursion?

The Chaco has rich fauna, but observing a particular species depends on location and conditions. For a dedicated bird- or wildlife-watching trip, choose a route with specialist local guiding.

### Where can I learn about the Chaco's history?

[Filadelfia](/paraguay/place/filadelfia/) is suitable for museums and the story of the colonies. Other stops depend on your interest in the Chaco War, nature or life in local communities.

## Tours through the Chaco: nature and history in western Paraguay

The [Chaco](/paraguay/place/chaco/) is an extensive region west of the Paraguay River. It differs sharply from [Asunción](/paraguay/place/asuncion/) and the green districts of eastern Paraguay: here are dry forests, open terrain, saline lagoons and small settlements. To appreciate the region, choose an itinerary with several stops instead of expecting a quick outing from the capital.

Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that cross the Chaco on their main routes. The [8-day Paraguay journey](/paraguay/tour/classic-paraguay-2023/) focuses on colonies, museums and Chaco War memorial sites. The [16-day journey through Uruguay, Paraguay and Iguazu](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/) combines regional history with a conservation centre, Laguna Capitán and a local community visit.

## What is the difference between the programmes?

| Programme | Chaco stops |
|---|---|
| [8 days in Paraguay](/paraguay/tour/classic-paraguay-2023/) | Filadelfia, Neuland, Boquerón, lagoon |
| [16 days including Uruguay](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/) | Fortín Toledo, lagoons, communities |

On the 8-day tour, the Chaco forms part of a journey entirely within Paraguay, after which the route continues through historic southern cities and Jesuit missions. On the 16-day tour, the region follows the Uruguay section; travellers then visit Guairá's green hills and Iguazu Falls.

### The Chaco on the 8-day journey

On day two, travellers leave [Asunción](/paraguay/place/asuncion/) and head to [Filadelfia](/paraguay/place/filadelfia/). Nature stops, a visit to an Indigenous village and the saline Laguna Capitán are scheduled along the way. The programme specifically notes that flamingos may gather at the lagoon in winter. Seeing the birds on a particular day cannot be guaranteed.

The following day is devoted to Filadelfia and the region's settlement history. Travellers visit the Jakob Unger Museum, [Neuland](/paraguay/place/neuland/) and Fort Boquerón, associated with the Chaco War of 1932–1935. A stop at the Pa'i Puku school is scheduled on day four on the road back to Asunción.

### The Chaco on the 16-day journey

In the [multi-country programme](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/), days eight, nine and ten take place in the Chaco. The road leads to Filadelfia, followed by [Fortín Toledo](/paraguay/place/fortin-toledo-reserve/), where nature conservation and Chaco War history are explored together. The conservation centre works to protect the tagua, a native peccary species.

The next day includes [Laguna Capitán](/paraguay/place/laguna-capitan/) and Mennonite settlements. On day ten, travellers visit an Indigenous Chaco community and the museum in Filadelfia before returning to Asunción. This part brings together the histories of settlers, Indigenous peoples and wildlife conservation.

## Why travellers visit the Chaco

**Nature and birds.** Dry forests, open woodland and saline lagoons reveal another side of South America. Conservation projects introduce travellers to peccaries and other local species. Wild animal sightings depend on season, weather and circumstances; a nature itinerary does not guarantee encounters with particular species. Travellers interested in different ecosystems may also like the [“Nature” catalogue](/interests/nature/).

**Settlement history.** [Filadelfia](/paraguay/place/filadelfia/) and [Neuland](/paraguay/place/neuland/) are associated with Mennonite migrants who built settlements, farms and cooperatives in conditions of limited water resources. Museums explain the development of the region; a visit to an Indigenous community introduces a different experience of life in the Chaco.

**War remembrance.** Forts, monuments and burial sites recall the conflict between Paraguay and Bolivia. The two routes feature different historical sites: Boquerón on the 8-day journey and [Fortín Toledo](/paraguay/place/fortin-toledo-reserve/) on the 16-day. These should not be treated as identical excursions.

## How much time should you allow and how should you prepare?

Exploring the Chaco involves lengthy drives between distant attractions. Compare not only total tour length but also **the number of days and overnight stays devoted specifically to western Paraguay**. [Filadelfia](/paraguay/place/filadelfia/) is an important stop on both routes, after which they return to [Asunción](/paraguay/place/asuncion/).

For this dry and hot region, bring water, sun protection and comfortable shoes. Dust, road conditions and weather need to be considered for lagoon visits and dirt-road sections. Check exact vehicles, accommodation, guides and included excursions in the chosen tour's terms.

If you want to contrast the dry Chaco with greener parts of Paraguay, the 16-day trip continues through [Colonia Independencia](/paraguay/place/colonia-independencia/) and the [Ybytyruzú Mountains](/paraguay/place/ybytyruzu-mountain-range/), with forest trails and hills.

## Frequently asked questions about Chaco tours

### Can I visit the Chaco on a day trip from Asunción?

Ada Tours' published Chaco programmes allocate several consecutive days, including the road journey to Filadelfia and the return to the capital. Neither programme provides a one-day option.

### Which tour focuses more on conservation areas?

The [16-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/) includes Fortín Toledo, Laguna Capitán and other Chaco natural sites. The [8-day trip](/paraguay/tour/classic-paraguay-2023/) also includes nature stops but gives greater emphasis to historic places and Mennonite colonies.

### Can you count on seeing flamingos?

No sightings can be guaranteed. Laguna Capitán is known for seasonal bird observations. Before travelling, consider the time of year and confirm the lagoon visit within the chosen itinerary.

### Which other areas of Paraguay can be combined with the Chaco?

Depending on the programme, you may visit Jesuit missions around [Encarnación and Trinidad](/paraguay/place/encarnacion-and-trinidad/), [Itaipu](/paraguay/place/itaipu/) or the nature routes of Guairá. Compare these in the [Paraguay tour catalogue](/paraguay/tour/).

## Ciudad del Este: what to see in Paraguay's city at the three borders

Ciudad del Este is in eastern [Paraguay](/paraguay/), in the Alto Paraná department. Across the Paraná River lies Foz do Iguaçu in Brazil, while the borders of Paraguay, Brazil and Argentina meet a little farther south. The city has become a major commercial centre, but its location also appeals to travellers combining several countries and the natural sights of the Paraná basin.

**Ciudad del Este's defining feature is the combination of a large border city with nearby natural and engineering attractions.** One itinerary could include shopping streets, the Friendship Bridge, Monday Falls and the Itaipu hydroelectric complex. These are separate places, however: city sightseeing, a waterfall excursion and an international border crossing all require their own time.

## Shopping streets, Friendship Bridge and the city centre

The city's history is connected with the development of eastern Paraguay and the construction of a crossing over the Paraná. Founded in 1957, the town was originally called Puerto Presidente Stroessner; it acquired its present name after the fall of the dictatorship. Today, trade attracts shoppers from neighbouring countries. Major shopping complexes selling electronics, clothing and other goods stand alongside small stores.

If shopping is your main purpose, decide in advance what you want to buy. Prices and stock differ among shops, while returns, warranties and customs formalities depend on the seller, goods and country of import. Check the final cost, paperwork and restrictions before paying. A city's location beside a border does not mean everything can be exported duty-free.

The Friendship Bridge connects Ciudad del Este with Foz do Iguaçu. It is both a landmark and an active international crossing with heavy traffic and pedestrian movement. The journey looks short on a map, but border formalities may take much longer than simply driving across the bridge.

For a quieter view of local life, leave the shopping streets for the Republic Lake, city squares and leisure areas. Here Ciudad del Este becomes more than a transit stop between the airport and Brazilian attractions.

## What to see around Ciudad del Este

| Attraction | Why visit |
|---|---|
| Friendship Bridge | Views of the Paraná and the link with Brazil |
| Monday Falls | Waterfalls and forest scenery |
| Itaipu | Hydropower engineering and the Paraná River |
| City centre | Shopping and everyday urban life |

**Monday Falls** lie in the neighbouring municipality of Presidente Franco, roughly 10 km from Ciudad del Este. The Monday River creates several powerful cascades. This is a separate nature stop, not an automatic part of every city visit. Check access hours, path conditions and possible weather-related restrictions beforehand.

**Itaipu Hydroelectric Dam** was built on the Paraná River as part of Paraguay and Brazil's shared energy infrastructure. It is a destination in its own right, not an ordinary viewpoint within the city centre. The available visiting programmes, document requirements and booking arrangements must be confirmed with the operator.

Ciudad del Este is also a useful base for exploring the [Brazilian side of Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and [Puerto Iguazú in Argentina](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). Iguazu Falls, Monday Falls and the Itaipu Dam are three different attractions. Each requires its own journey and possibly a border crossing.

## Getting there and allocating time

If you pass through Ciudad del Este on your way to Brazil, a short city stop may suffice. Shopping calls for additional time, while the nature sites of eastern Paraguay deserve a full day or longer, depending on your chosen stops and transport.

When arriving from Foz do Iguaçu, check entry and return rules for your nationality, transit conditions, passport-validity requirements and vehicle documents. Permission to enter one country does not guarantee entry into its neighbour. During busy shopping periods and holidays, allow extra travel time rather than scheduling a tight international flight connection after the border crossing.

Eastern Paraguay has a warm, humid climate, and heavy rain may affect walking and traffic. Comfortable shoes and sun protection are useful in the city; near waterfalls, bring clothing that can get wet from spray.

## Ciudad del Este on Ada Tours itineraries

On our [16-day journey through Uruguay and Paraguay](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/), Ciudad del Este serves as an arrival point by air and a transfer stop en route to Iguazu. The programme visits several Paraguayan regions, but mentioning Ciudad del Este does not establish that shopping, Monday Falls or an Itaipu excursion are included.

If you would like an additional day here, discuss it separately from the necessary border crossings. Start with the [Paraguay destination page](/paraguay/) and the wider tour geography; actual stops are determined by the selected programme.

## Frequently asked questions about Ciudad del Este

### Are Ciudad del Este and Foz do Iguaçu one city?

No. Ciudad del Este is in Paraguay, while Foz do Iguaçu is in Brazil. They are linked by the Friendship Bridge across the Paraná, which is also an international border crossing.

### Can Monday Falls and Iguazu Falls be visited on one trip?

Yes, provided you allow for separate transfers and any required border crossings. Monday Falls are near Ciudad del Este, while Iguazu Falls are visited from Brazil and Argentina. These are different natural attractions.

### Is it worth spending a night in Ciudad del Este?

An overnight stay is not always necessary for a short transit. It becomes more useful if you plan to shop, visit Monday Falls or Itaipu or reduce the risk of delays after crossing the border. The appropriate duration depends on the actual itinerary, not just map distance.

## Tours through Ciudad del Este: Itaipu or the road to Iguazu

[Ciudad del Este](/paraguay/place/ciudad-del-este/) stands in eastern Paraguay on the Paraná River near the Brazilian border. It is known for its shopping districts and proximity to the [Itaipu Hydroelectric Dam](/paraguay/place/itaipu/). From here, travellers can continue to the area where Paraguay, Brazil and Argentina meet.

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Ciudad del Este on the main route. Yet **the city's role in the two programmes differs**. The [8-day Paraguay tour](/paraguay/tour/classic-paraguay-2023/) includes an overnight stay here and an excursion to Itaipu the following day. The [16-day journey through Uruguay, Paraguay and Iguazu](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/) uses the city to continue across the border into Brazil.

## Two ways to include the city in a journey

| Tour | Role of the city |
|---|---|
| [8 days in Paraguay](/paraguay/tour/classic-paraguay-2023/) | Overnight stay, Itaipu, return to the capital |
| [16-day multi-country tour](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/) | Arrival and onward transfer into Brazil |

### The eight-day Paraguay tour

On day six, travellers head from the south of the country through the Jesuit mission region to Ciudad del Este. Previously, the itinerary explores [Encarnación and Trinidad](/paraguay/place/encarnacion-and-trinidad/) and [Jesús](/paraguay/place/jesus/), where the heritage of Jesuit settlements survives. Accommodation at a hotel in Ciudad del Este is included.

Day seven features a visit to the memorial to scientist Moisés Bertoni and the [Itaipu Hydroelectric Dam](/paraguay/place/itaipu/). Approximately an hour and a half is allocated to the dam visit on this tour. After the excursions, travellers return to [Asunción](/paraguay/place/asuncion/). This suits visitors who want to see a major engineering site and finish their journey in Paraguay.

### The sixteen-day tour including Uruguay and Iguazu

On the [16-day programme](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/), Ciudad del Este features on day thirteen after travel through the [Chaco](/paraguay/place/chaco/) and [Colonia Independencia](/paraguay/place/colonia-independencia/). The day includes a flight to Ciudad del Este and onward travel to Foz do Iguaçu in Brazil.

Day fourteen visits the Brazilian side of Iguazu Falls, and day fifteen the Argentine side. The city therefore functions as a connecting point. **Neither a shopping tour nor a visit to Itaipu is listed on this itinerary**. Such activities require extra time and a separate agreement.

## What to see in the city and nearby

Ciudad del Este is an important trading centre on Paraguay's eastern border. The Friendship Bridge across the Paraná connects it to Foz do Iguaçu in Brazil. Its markets, shops and busy streets differ greatly from nature stops in the [Chaco](/paraguay/place/chaco/) and historic sites of southern Paraguay.

The main confirmed attraction near the city on the [8-day tour](/paraguay/tour/classic-paraguay-2023/) is [Itaipu](/paraguay/place/itaipu/), the joint Paraguay–Brazil energy complex. Tourist visits to the dam and access rules must be confirmed for the chosen date, as a major engineering facility may offer several different visiting routes.

The three-border region also offers opportunities to travel into neighbouring countries. However, staying overnight on the Paraguayan side does not itself include a journey to Brazil or Argentina. Each border crossing requires time, a route and appropriate documents.

## Planning borders and transfers

The two tours have different logistics. On the 8-day itinerary, travellers return to Asunción after visiting Itaipu. On the 16-day tour, after arriving in Ciudad del Este, accommodation and excursions belong to the Brazilian part of the journey.

When crossing the border, consider every traveller's citizenship and passport, current entry rules, immigration queues and possible delays on the bridge. Visa conditions depend on the passport and number of entries; check official requirements for the specific trip. One set of documents cannot automatically be assumed sufficient for all three countries.

If you want to add shopping, an independent walk in Ciudad del Este or another excursion, discuss it when selecting the route. You will need free time, transport and confirmation that the addition works with subsequent transfers. The [general Paraguay tours catalogue](/paraguay/tour/) allows comparison of single-country and multi-country options.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Ciudad del Este

### Does every tour through the city include Itaipu?

No. The [8-day programme](/paraguay/tour/classic-paraguay-2023/) includes a visit to [Itaipu](/paraguay/place/itaipu/). On the [16-day tour](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/), the city is used as a transfer point towards Iguazu Falls on the Brazilian side.

### Where do visitors spend the night in Ciudad del Este?

On the 8-day itinerary, a hotel in the city is scheduled for day six. On the 16-day tour, travellers continue into Brazil after reaching Ciudad del Este, so an overnight stay on the Paraguayan side cannot be promised from that description.

### Is there time to visit shops?

Ciudad del Este is known for commerce, but shopping time and accompanied shopping are not specified on these itineraries. If shopping is a priority, request it separately.

### Are documents needed to cross into Brazil?

Requirements depend on citizenship and current entry rules. A border crossing is part of the 16-day programme; check the documents before choosing dates and flights. Being in Paraguay does not automatically give you permission to enter Brazil.

## Colonia Independencia: German heritage and the nature of Guairá

Colonia Independencia (Independencia) is located in the Guairá department of eastern [Paraguay](/paraguay/). Green hills, forest roads, streams and waterfalls surround it, all associated with the [Ybytyruzú Mountain Range](/paraguay/place/ybytyruzu-mountain-range/). The area introduces both eastern Paraguay's natural environment and the history of European settler communities.

Unlike [Asunción](/paraguay/place/asuncion/) or the drier Chaco region, a visit to Guairá revolves around smaller roads and rural stops. Attractions are spread out, so it is better to select particular walking trails and natural landmarks than try to visit every hill during one brief stop.

## Why is German heritage so visible in Colonia Independencia?

According to Paraguay's national tourism portal, the colony was founded on **January 17, 1919**, by German settlers after the First World War. Over time, cultural traditions developed here, with European influences evident in local architecture, celebrations and agriculture.

The settlement's centre is known as **Melgarejo**. It serves as a point of orientation for local life and the starting point for journeys into the natural surroundings. Colonia Independencia and Independencia refer to the same district, while Melgarejo is its central settlement.

Another local tradition is **artisan winemaking**, which developed alongside the settlements. It is important to distinguish cultural history from a specific tourism product. The presence of wineries does not mean that a tasting is available without arrangement on any given day. Actual visiting conditions depend on the winery and selected programme.

## Which waterfalls and mountains are nearby?

The main nature area is the [Ybytyruzú Mountains](/paraguay/place/ybytyruzu-mountain-range/), with wooded slopes, streams, trails and viewpoints. Guairá's regional authorities identify several mountain routes and waterfalls as attractions.

**Salto Suizo** lies in a forested area nearby. Visiting the falls often involves a walk in natural terrain. After heavy rain, earth and stones can be slippery, while road access may differ from the dry season. Confirm the actual trail and entry conditions before travelling.

**Cerro Tres Kandú** is Paraguay's highest summit at about **842 metres** above sea level. Climbing it is a separate active journey. Its presence in the area does not make it part of every Colonia Independencia visit. Plan the time, physical effort, guide arrangements and access rules before an ascent.

**Cerro Akatĩ and other Ybytyruzú hills** attract visitors for panoramic views and nature walks. Access differs between sections of the range: some can be reached by road, while others require a full hike.

| Interest | Where to go |
|---|---|
| Waterfalls | Salto Suizo |
| Panoramas | Ybytyruzú hills |
| Trekking | Tres Kandú |
| Culture | Melgarejo |

## Dividing your time between nature and rural culture

For a short introduction, choose one natural landmark and complement it with a walk through the settlement or a visit to a particular farm. Several trails, waterfalls and a summit climb require a more flexible plan allowing for roads, weather and the time needed to return.

A nature day and a cultural visit involve different arrangements. The former calls for appropriate shoes, water, a rain forecast and trail conditions; the latter requires a prearranged visit to a local site or producer. Both can fit into a journey if the day is not filled entirely with transfers.

Mountain weather differs from conditions in the capital. Rain and cloud cover affect trail access and views from slopes. For climbs, check the conditions of the specific section rather than relying solely on the national forecast.

## Colonia Independencia on Ada Tours itineraries

On our published [16-day journey through Uruguay and Paraguay](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/), the nature section in Guairá follows visits to the capital and the Chaco. It includes a stop near Colonia Independencia, walks in the [Ybytyruzú Mountains](/paraguay/place/ybytyruzu-mountain-range/) and an introduction to German settlements and artisan winemaking.

**Climbing Tres Kandú is not listed as compulsory.** The itinerary introduces the mountain area but is not a dedicated sporting hike to the country's highest point. If you want that climb, it must be considered as a separate part of the trip.

After Guairá, the journey continues to [Ciudad del Este](/paraguay/place/ciudad-del-este/) and Iguazu. In one itinerary, the dry Chaco, green hills and humid border regions follow one another. Other options can be found in the [Paraguay tour catalogue](/paraguay/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about Colonia Independencia

### Where is Colonia Independencia?

In the Guairá department of eastern Paraguay, near the [Ybytyruzú](/paraguay/place/ybytyruzu-mountain-range/) mountain area.

### When was Colonia Independencia founded?

January 17, 1919. Its founders were German settlers whose cultural legacy remains visible in the district.

### Which natural sites can be visited?

Nearby are Salto Suizo, Cerro Tres Kandú and other Ybytyruzú hills and waterfalls. Check road, trail and access conditions for each excursion.

### Does the 16-day Ada Tours tour include a climb of Tres Kandú?

No. That ascent is not listed as a compulsory part of the programme. The [tour](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/) visits Guairá and its mountain area, while a sporting climb requires separate arrangement.
